(a) In General.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report on the compliance of the Department of Veterans Affairs with industry standards for caskets and urns. 
    (b) Elements.—The report required by subsection (a) shall include the following:
        (1) A description of industry standards for caskets and urns. 
        (2) An assessment of compliance with such standards at national cemeteries administered by the Department with respect to caskets and urns used for the interment of those eligible for burial at such cemeteries.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a formal report on "industry standards" brings industry into the process. It does not: the section only requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to report to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. No consultation with industry, the public, states, or any other outside party is required, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report

opus.w: The only formal interaction here is a report from a federal official to congressional committees, and that stays inside the federal government. The mention of "industry standards" might suggest industry is involved. However, the Secretary only describes and assesses those standards. No industry group, outside expert or member of the public is consulted before a federal decision.
opus.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report on the compliance of the Department of Veterans Affairs with industry standards for caskets and urns.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with non-federal entities, or an advisory board with outside members.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs shall submit to the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs of the House of Representatives a report on the compliance of the Department of Veterans Affairs with industry standards for caskets and urns.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report assesses "industry standards," it implicitly involves consultation with industry experts. However, the text only mandates the submission of a report to Congress. It does not explicitly require the Secretary to consult with outside parties, nor does it establish a public comment period or advisory board for this specific task. The definition states that reports to Congress are inside the federal government and do not constitute participation.
